cards.title: Task · Find duplicates
cards.summary: Interview prompt: find business-key values that occur more than once.

entries.meaning: Group by the key and keep only groups whose row count is greater than one.
entries.detail:
SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS copies
FROM users
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

entries.meaning: GROUP BY creates one group per key; HAVING filters after aggregation.
entries.detail: Use the real uniqueness rule: one column or the full composite business key.

more.meaning: Duplicate means the whole key repeats, not just one component.
more.detail: GROUP BY first_name, last_name, birth_date HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

more.meaning: Decide whether unknown values belong in the duplicate check.
more.detail: WHERE email IS NOT NULL  -- add when NULL should not form a duplicate group

cards.title: Task · Return every duplicate row
cards.summary: GROUP BY shows duplicate keys; this pattern returns the actual offending rows.

entries.meaning: Count rows inside each key partition, then filter in an outer query.
Window values are produced after WHERE, so filter them one query level later.
entries.detail: CTE / derived table → compute window result → outer WHERE

cards.title: Task · Deduplicate safely
cards.summary: Identify exactly which rows are duplicates before running dialect-specific DELETE syntax.

entries.meaning: Rank each duplicate group; rn = 1 is the survivor and rn > 1 are removal candidates.
ORDER BY must choose one deterministic survivor.
entries.detail: ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC

more.meaning: Delete only the previewed primary keys, inside a transaction; DELETE-from-CTE syntax differs by engine.
more.detail: BEGIN → preview IDs → DELETE by primary key → verify counts → COMMIT / ROLLBACK

cards.title: Task · Latest row per entity
cards.summary: Return the newest order, event, status, or version for every entity.

entries.meaning: Number rows newest-first inside each entity and keep row 1.
MAX(created_at) alone returns only a timestamp and can match multiple tied rows.
entries.detail: Add a stable secondary key such as id DESC.

cards.title: Task · Second-highest distinct value
cards.summary: Classic interview task: return the second distinct salary, score, or amount.

entries.meaning: DENSE_RANK ranks equal values together and does not leave gaps between distinct values.
For exactly the second value, compare against the maximum.
entries.detail:
SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees
WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees);

cards.title: Task · Nth-highest distinct value
cards.summary: Generalize the second-highest problem while handling ties correctly.

entries.meaning: Rank distinct value groups and filter by the requested rank.
Use ROW_NUMBER only when every row should occupy a different position; use DENSE_RANK for distinct-value ranking.
entries.detail: ties: ROW_NUMBER → separate positions · DENSE_RANK → same position

cards.title: Task · Top N per group
cards.summary: Return the top three products per category, employees per team, or scores per user.

entries.meaning: Partition by the group, order by the metric, then filter the generated row number.
Use RANK or DENSE_RANK when tied metric values should all qualify.
entries.detail: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY revenue DESC)

cards.title: Task · Find entities with no related rows
cards.summary: Find customers without orders, users without profiles, or test cases without executions.

entries.meaning: Use an anti-semi pattern with NOT EXISTS.
NOT EXISTS avoids the NULL trap that can make NOT IN evaluate to unknown.
entries.detail: Prefer NOT EXISTS when the subquery key may contain NULL.

more.meaning: Equivalent when the joined key is non-NULL and the intent is clear.
more.detail: LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.id IS NULL

cards.title: Task · Find orphan child rows
cards.summary: Data-quality task: locate child records whose referenced parent does not exist.

entries.meaning: Start from the child table and reject rows that have a matching parent.
Useful after imports, disabled constraints, migrations, or ETL loads.
entries.detail: Expected result in an integrity check: 0 rows.

cards.title: Task · Compare expected vs actual data
cards.summary: Find rows present in the expected result but missing or different in the actual result.

entries.meaning: EXCEPT returns distinct rows from the left result that are absent from the right result.
Run EXCEPT in both directions to detect both missing and unexpected rows.
entries.detail:
expected EXCEPT actual
UNION ALL
actual EXCEPT expected

more.meaning: Plain EXCEPT is distinct-set comparison; validate duplicate counts separately when multiplicity matters.

cards.title: Task · Running total
cards.summary: Calculate cumulative balance, revenue, defects, or executions without collapsing rows.

entries.meaning: Use SUM as a window aggregate ordered by the sequence of events.
entries.detail:
SELECT account_id, occurred_at, amount,
       SUM(amount) OVER (
         PARTITION BY account_id
         ORDER BY occurred_at, id
         ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
       ) AS running_total
FROM ledger;

entries.meaning: An explicit ROWS frame avoids peer-group surprises when several rows share the same ordering value.
entries.detail: Use a deterministic ORDER BY, usually timestamp + primary key.

cards.title: Task · Compare with the previous row
cards.summary: Detect a change in status, price, count, or measurement between consecutive events.

entries.meaning: LAG exposes a value from the previous row in the window ordering.
LAG returns NULL when no previous row exists unless a default is supplied.
entries.detail: Handle the first row explicitly when NULL is also a valid business value.

cards.title: Task · Find gaps in a sequence
cards.summary: Detect missing IDs, invoice numbers, versions, or ordered event sequence values.

entries.meaning: Compare each sequence value with its predecessor.
entries.detail:
WITH x AS (
  SELECT sequence_no,
         LAG(sequence_no) OVER (ORDER BY sequence_no) AS prev_no
  FROM events
)
SELECT prev_no + 1 AS gap_start, sequence_no - 1 AS gap_end
FROM x
WHERE sequence_no > prev_no + 1;

entries.meaning: This checks numeric continuity, not whether every generated identifier must legally exist.
entries.detail: Define the expected sequence rule before treating a gap as a defect.

cards.title: Task · Count several conditions in one query
cards.summary: Produce pass/fail/error counts or status KPIs without multiple scans or queries.

entries.meaning: Turn each condition into 1 or 0 and aggregate it.
entries.detail:
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'passed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed,
  SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'error'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS errors
FROM test_results;

entries.meaning: Add GROUP BY to calculate the same metrics per build, suite, team, or day.
entries.detail: GROUP BY build_id

cards.title: Task · No activity since a cutoff
cards.summary: Find users or entities with no qualifying event in a given period without dialect-specific date arithmetic.

entries.meaning: Pass the cutoff as a parameter and use NOT EXISTS against qualifying activity.
entries.detail:
SELECT u.*
FROM users u
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM events e
  WHERE e.user_id = u.id
    AND e.occurred_at >= :cutoff
);

entries.meaning: Date-add/subtract syntax differs by dialect; computing the cutoff outside the query keeps the core pattern portable.
entries.detail: :cutoff = application/test parameter

cards.title: Task · Detect join multiplication
cards.summary: Find parent rows that multiply after a join because the relationship is one-to-many or the join key is incomplete.

entries.meaning: Count joined rows per expected parent key and inspect groups with more than one match.
entries.detail:
SELECT p.id, COUNT(*) AS joined_rows
FROM parents p
JOIN children c ON c.parent_id = p.id
GROUP BY p.id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

entries.meaning: Multiple rows may be correct for 1:N; the defect is assuming 1:1 or omitting part of a composite join key.
entries.detail: Check relationship cardinality before adding DISTINCT.

cards.title: Task · Stable next-page query
cards.summary: Use the last seen sort key instead of scanning an ever-growing OFFSET.

entries.meaning: Continue strictly after the last row using the same deterministic sort keys.
entries.detail:
WHERE created_at < :last_created_at
   OR (created_at = :last_created_at AND id < :last_id)
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC

entries.meaning: Apply the dialect's normal row-limiting syntax after the predicate.
entries.detail: PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite: LIMIT 50 · SQL Server: TOP / OFFSET-FETCH

more.meaning: The cursor columns and ORDER BY must match, and the ordering must be unique enough to avoid skips or repeats.
more.detail: timestamp alone is usually insufficient → add id

cards.title: Task · Percent of total
cards.summary: Calculate each group's contribution while keeping one result row per group.

entries.meaning: Aggregate each group, then window-sum those aggregate results for the denominator.
entries.detail:
SELECT category_id,
       SUM(amount) AS amount,
       100.0 * SUM(amount)
         / NULLIF(SUM(SUM(amount)) OVER (), 0) AS pct_total
FROM sales
GROUP BY category_id;

entries.meaning: NULLIF prevents division by zero when the total is zero.
entries.detail: NULLIF(total, 0)
